title: The Pair, pilot 2: a calculator with a split spec
task: Create calc.js (CommonJS) exporting evaluate(expr): it takes an arithmetic expression as a string and returns its value as a number. Numbers, + - * /, parentheses and spaces must work; invalid input throws an Error. That's all the spec you have; your navigator knows the product's other requirements. Use only Node's standard library.
navigator_notes:
1. ^ is power and is right-associative: 2^3^2 is 512.
2. Unary minus binds looser than ^: -2^2 is -4, but 2^-1 is 0.5. It can repeat: --3 is 3.
3. % is not modulo. It is a postfix percent on a number or a parenthesised group. When it is the right-hand operand of + or -, it means that percent of the left-hand side: 200+10% is 220, 50-10% is 45. Anywhere else it divides by 100: 10% is 0.1, 50*10% is 5, (10+10)% is 0.2.
4. Division by zero throws an Error whose message contains "division by zero".
5. Every syntax error throws an Error whose message contains "at N", where N is the 0-based index of the character where it went wrong (the end of the string if input ran out): "1+*2" says at 2, "1 2" says at 2, "(1+2" says at 4, "" says at 0.
6. Numbers can be written 5, 0.5, .5 or 5. but scientific notation is not allowed: "1e3" is a syntax error (at 1).
